data.narrative:
CubeFabs is a Series E semiconductor company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, CEO; former Columbia materials science professor) and his father John Putman. The target operates within a competitive frontier-chip landscape alongside 8 private peers (including Etched, Cerebras, and Credo Semiconductor) and 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Valuation analysis relies primarily on stage-progression methodology, given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $182M as a baseline proxy and applying a typical Series E-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.4x yields an implied valuation of $255M. A peer-median approach was not feasible: while 12 same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, similar tier) produced three or more comparable datapoints, rendering sector-wide aggregation unreliable. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple—where the three semiconductor public comparables trade at a 21.0x median—cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely release.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $217M to $293M, centered on $255M. The narrow methodological foundation—reliance on a single applicable technique—is the primary limitation. Sensitivity extends upward if the step-up multiplier exceeds 1.4x or if revenue-based anchoring becomes feasible; downside risk exists if the target's burn rate, capital efficiency, or market traction trail peer norms. Resolution of these uncertainties would require either revenue disclosure or expanded comparable-company depth.
